architecture.title: The Hotel Ops Ensemble — who holds what, and where text crosses a trust boundary
architecture.caption: Guests and staff talk to the orchestrator, which routes each request to one specialist. The energy agent holds the two tools that change the building; the maintenance agent talks to another company's agent over A2A after finding its Agent Card in a directory. Every tool call passes one policy enforcement point (PEP), which checks nothing until you switch controls on. Each arrow is a trust boundary: text written by someone else arriving in an agent's context. (week28_maestro_mas_security/common/ensemble.py — simulated.)

sequence.title: A03 — one guest sentence travels two hops to a tool
sequence.caption: Captured from Lab 01-2 (SIM brain). The orchestrator forwards the guest's text verbatim to the concierge; the concierge 'tells the energy agent'; the energy agent receives a short, clean instruction and runs it. Only the principal tag [for guest:1203] still shows who started it. With every defense on, the orchestrator forwards only an allow-listed task and the instruction never leaves the front door.
